description: 2 tactical challenges for White in the Alekhine-Chatard Attack. Play 6.h4! and launch the kingside pawn storm.

drills.briefExplanation: 6.h4! O-O 7.Bd3 c5 8.dxc5 — launch the storm, then open the center.
drills.description: White to play. Black retreated 5...Nfd7 — launch the Alekhine-Chatard with 6.h4!.
drills.explanation: The Alekhine-Chatard Attack: White plays the startling 6.h4!, preparing h5 to rip open Black's kingside. After 6...O-O 7.Bd3 White's attack builds with every move — h5, Qh5, Bxh7 ideas. The French's solid center means nothing when the kingside is under direct assault. Pawn storms beat pawn chains.
drills.name: The h4 Launch

drills.briefExplanation: 7.Bd3 c5 8.Nb5! a6 9.Nd6 — challenge the break, leap, and occupy the hole.
drills.description: White to play. Black countered 7...c5 — leap 8.Nb5! toward the weak squares.
drills.explanation: Against Black's 7...c5 break, White doesn't retreat — 8.Nb5! leaps toward d6, and after 8...a6 comes 9.Nd6!, occupying the hole in Black's camp. The knight eyes f7 and e8, Black's development stalls, and White's initiative is overwhelming.
drills.name: The Nb5 Leap

name: Alekhine-Chatard Attack — White Tactics
